description:
Found by the fz-kdt.199 cold review (2026-09-03, base ca23b676f), with three
reproducers; named in that ticket as the owner of its edge-set gap.

fz-kdt.199`s `returned` axis is solved over the SAME forwarding cone as
fz-kdt.183`s `forwarded_dispatch`, i.e. over `forwarded_inputs`. That edge set
has three holes, and the returned axis inherits all of them:

1. It ignores `LoweredTail::DirectCall`s `dest`. Reproducer deliver2.fz (a body
   that returns the constant `0`): keys go 7 -> 9 executables, a split that
   buys nothing, purely because the delivery edge is invisible.
2. A RECONSTRUCTED argument is not a forward edge. Reproducer hops.fz: `outer/2`
   stays collapsed while `inner/2` and `mid/2` split, so two keys naming
   `list(binary)` and `list(int)` BOTH publish the join -- 2 executables for 0
   precision, and the wrong diagnostic survives.
3. A PROJECTED argument is not a forward edge, so the protocol-callback case
   stays broken. Reproducer proto_cb.fz.

These are the same class fz-kdt.183 left behind (a Tuple CONSTRUCTION handed to
a self-call is opaque to the rule), now inherited by the return side. The cure
is one edge-set improvement serving both axes: teach the cone about a
DirectCall dest, a reconstruction whose fields trace to clause params, and a
projection.

CONCORDANT: fz-kdt.183 (the cone this extends), fz-kdt.199 (the axis that
inherits the holes), fz-kdt.165 (the identity axis planned on the SAME cone
walk -- it will inherit them too, so fixing the edge set once serves three
axes).

RED-FIRST: deliver2.fz keys 7 not 9; hops.fz`s outer/2 splits so neither key
publishes a join; proto_cb.fz gets the correct per-implementation return.
title: The returned axis reuses forwarded_inputs, which ignores a DirectCall dest and does not see reconstructed or projected arguments
